stick_photography_exposure_reciprocity_a.question: Photography - exposure, reciprocity, angle of view, hyperfocal
references: ISO 2720:1974 - exposure meters and the APEX system (EV = log2(N^2/t) at ISO 100)
Kodak, the sunny-16 rule (film data sheets, 20th c.)
R. Kingslake, Optics in Photography (SPIE, 1992), ch. 4 and 5
H. M. Merklinger, The INs and OUTs of FOCUS (1992) - depth of field and hyperfocal
stick_photography_exposure_reciprocity_a.statement: A camera's settings are logarithms and tangents: EV counts stops in base 2, the angle of view is 2 atan(d/2f), and the hyperfocal distance is f^2/(N c) + f.

ticks.claim: [EV at f/8, 1/250, SEALED] EV = log2(64 x 250) = 13.97 (sealed through photography.PHOTO_VERIFY): the APEX scale, each unit one stop - a doubling of light.

[sunny 16, SEALED] f/16 at 1/125 (the nearest click to 1/ISO at ISO 100) is EV 14.97, EV 15 (sealed through photography.PHOTO_VERIFY): the rule of thumb for direct sun, which is why a light meter reads 15 on a clear noon.

[reciprocity, SEALED] f/8 at 1/250 and f/11 at 1/125 are equivalent exposures (sealed through photography.PHOTO_VERIFY): one stop closed, one stop longer, the same light. f/11 is the nominal name of 8 sqrt 2 = 11.31; the 0.09 EV difference is the rounding of the f-stop series, inside the verifier's 0.1 EV window.

[one stop apart, SEALED AS NOT EQUIVALENT] f/8 at 1/250 and f/8 at 1/125 differ by one stop - sealed with claimed_equivalent = false (sealed through photography.PHOTO_VERIFY). Twice the time at the same aperture is twice the light; the engine seals the inequality as an inequality.

[the normal lens, SEALED] 50 mm on a 36 mm frame sees 2 atan(36 / 100) = 39.6 deg across (sealed through photography.PHOTO_VERIFY) - the horizontal angle of the 'normal' lens, roughly the angle of comfortable attention.
[wide, SEALED] 24 mm sees 73.7 deg (sealed through photography.PHOTO_VERIFY).

[long, SEALED] 200 mm sees 10.3 deg (sealed through photography.PHOTO_VERIFY): the tangent is nearly linear here, so the angle falls almost as 1/f - four times the focal length, nearly a quarter of the angle.
[hyperfocal at 50 mm f/8, SEALED] H = 50^2 / (8 x 0.030) + 50 = 10,467 mm = 10.47 m (sealed through photography.PHOTO_VERIFY). Focus there and everything from 5.2 m to infinity is acceptably sharp.
[at 24 mm f/8, SEALED] H = 576 / 0.24 + 24 = 2.42 m (sealed through photography.PHOTO_VERIFY): the square of the focal length is why wide lenses carry so much depth of field.

[the conventions, CITED] EV at ISO 100 is the APEX convention (ISO 2720); the f-stop series 1, 1.4, 2, 2.8, 4, 5.6, 8, 11, 16 names powers of sqrt 2 rounded; the 0.030 mm circle of confusion is a convention for a 36 mm frame viewed as an 8 x 10 print at arm's length - another viewer, another number. Cited, never sealed; the arithmetic they command is what is sealed.
ticks.source: ISO 2720:1974; Kingslake, Optics in Photography (1992); Merklinger (1992)

ticks.claim: [on the one map] A camera is applied optics (card_floor_optics: the thin lens, the aperture, the circle of confusion) counted in logarithms (card_floor_logarithm: EV is a base-2 scale, every unit a doubling). The optics stick holds the lens; this stick holds the exposure.
